question: Article 6 of the Italian Government’s ‘Energy’ decree interprets Article 56(3a) of Legislative Decree No 270 of 8 July 1999 – an act already repealed for being inconsistent with EU law: Law No 270/1999 was converted by Law No 166/2009, following CJEU judgments.

The article in question sets out the provisions on authentic interpretation in the event of the transfer of ongoing businesses by companies that are the subject of an extraordinary administration procedure, and provides that the transactions concerned are those performed with a view to the liquidation of the assets of the transferor; transfers performed in implementation of the liquidation programme do not constitute transfers of an undertaking, a subsidiary or part of an undertaking, where they are performed on the basis of Commission decisions excluding economic continuity between transferor and transferee ‘in accordance with Article 5(1) of Directive 2001/23/EC’.

However, the CJEU asserted the need for a narrow interpretation of Article 5 to better protect workers, thereby upholding the principle that wherever continuity of business enterprise is concerned, Article 2112 of the Italian Civil Code should be applied; this new law lays down the applicable rules, substituting the provisions of Article 56 referred to above.
Can the Commission say whether it considers this new article to conform to EU rules, in the light of CJEU judgments, and in particular C-561/07?
answer: The Honourable Members ask the Commission to assess a potential contradiction between Article 6 of Decree-law n.131 of 29 September 2023 (1) and Directive 2001/23/EC (2) in the light of the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union (‘the Court’), more particularly, of its judgment of 11 June 2009, Commission v Italy, C-561/07.

It must be underlined that, while the case mentioned referred to a national procedure ‘designed to promote the continuation of its business with a view to its subsequent recovery’, the situation regulated in Article 6 of Decree-law n.131/2023, refers to procedures which, in principle, are ‘carried out with a view to the liquidation of the assets of the transferor’.

The judgment of the Court is therefore not relevant to the situation governed by Article 6 of Decree-law n.131/2023 and it does not provide enough elements to conclude that Article 6 of Decree-law n.131/2023 is contrary to Directive 2001/23/EC.

Decreto-legge 29 settembre 2023, n. 131 Misure urgenti in materia di energia, interventi per sostenere il potere di acquisto e a tutela del risparmio. (GU Serie Generale n.228 del 29-09-2023). Council Directive 2001/23/EC of 12 March 2001 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of undertakings or businesses (OJ L 82, 22.3.2001, p. 16-20).
